changed.new_text: A habit has at most one non-deleted check-in per date; another one with a new id answers 409 with code `duplicate_check_in`.
changed.old_text: A habit has at most one non-deleted check-in per date; another one with a new id answers 409 with code `already_checked_in`.

changed.new_text: A batch processes its items in order, each exactly as a single check-in create would, and answers 200 `{results: [{id, status, code?, completion?}, ...]}` in the items' order, where `status` is `created` (with the completion), `existing` (an identical retry, with the completion) or `rejected` (with the `code` the single create would answer, e.g. `not_found`, `date_too_old`, `duplicate_check_in`, `id_conflict`).
changed.old_text: A batch processes its items in order, each exactly as a single check-in create would, and answers 200 `{results: [{id, status, code?, completion?}, ...]}` in the items' order, where `status` is `created` (with the completion), `existing` (an identical retry, with the completion) or `rejected` (with the `code` the single create would answer, e.g. `not_found`, `date_too_old`, `already_checked_in`, `id_conflict`).

summary.note: Which workflows fail is mostly not decidable before the change exists: a flow records the answers the app gives today, so it passes today by construction. Before an implementation only a changed invariant (tier 1, observed) and an exact-prefix contradiction (tier 2, determined) decide a workflow; every other flow listed is tier 3 'may_fail' (static, with unknowns), settled by tier 4 (Spike E, observed after the change).
